project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to be focused on educational management, likely related to exam processes, student information, and potentially course enrollment. The dependency graph reveals a tiered structure, with core components like layouts and common UI elements alongside specific views representing various exam and result functionalities.  The project demonstrates a moderate level of complexity, managing user interactions and data presentation across several related modules.  The presence of distinct views for different exam phases and result displays indicates a phased approach to managing student assessments.

layers.description: Handles user interface rendering and interaction logic.
Manages application navigation and component transitions.
Handles data fetching, processing, and potentially integrations with backend services.

macro_trends.title: Potential UI/UX Redundancy
macro_trends.description: Several files (e.g., iLike-* views, ResultPage.vue) seem to be focused on specific user experiences within the application. Consolidation and/or component reuse could improve maintainability. Further investigation is needed to understand the intended use and scope of each view.

macro_trends.title: Route-Driven Component Hierarchy
macro_trends.description: The dependency graph is heavily driven by router navigation. While functional, this creates a very rigid component structure. Consideration should be given to alternative navigation patterns or data flow techniques.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow involves navigating through the forms to capture exam submission details, validating data, and ultimately persisting the results. It relies on several components like ExamFormSubmission.vue, FeeDetails.vue, and ResultPage.vue, highlighting a core business process.

key_workflows.name: User Interaction & Course Discovery
key_workflows.description: The iLike-* views represent a user-centric workflow for course discovery and engagement. This flow starts with the user exploring different courses and potentially submitting feedback, relying on components like iLikeCourses.vue, iLikeDashboard.vue, and iLikeLanding.vue.
